security_audit.summary: Static analysis misclassified 48 Markdown backticks as command execution and six benign documentation values as network, environment, or reconnaissance risks. The fixed local download path can overwrite a file. Deletion examples can remove registry data, and the automated cleanup loop lacks an explicit confirmation gate.

remediation.issue: Repository, tag, and manifest deletion examples can permanently remove remote registry data.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation, show a dry run, and verify registry identity, resource names, tags, and digests before deletion.

remediation.issue: The blob download example writes to a fixed path and can overwrite an existing local file.
remediation.suggestion: Accept an explicit destination, reject existing files by default, and validate the download before replacing any file.

content.user_title: Manage Azure Container Registry with Python
content.value_statement: Managing repository metadata, manifests, tags, and blobs through the Azure SDK requires precise API usage. This skill provides focused Python patterns for common registry operations.
actual_capabilities: Creates authenticated clients with DefaultAzureCredential and anonymous clients for public registries.
Lists repositories, image tags, and manifests with ordering options.
Reads and updates repository and manifest properties.
Deletes repositories, tags, and manifests through SDK methods.
Downloads manifests and layer blobs to local storage.
Shows asynchronous repository listing and age-based cleanup patterns.
limitations: The skill provides examples and guidance, not a packaged automation tool.
Examples require the Azure Container Registry and Azure Identity Python packages.
Remote changes require suitable Azure permissions and can cause data loss.
The artifact section demonstrates downloads but does not demonstrate uploads.

use_cases.title: Inspect Registry Inventory
use_cases.description: List repositories, tags, and manifests, then review dates, sizes, digests, and metadata.

use_cases.title: Protect Production Artifacts
use_cases.description: Update repository and manifest properties to prevent unintended writes or deletion.

use_cases.title: Plan Registry Cleanup
use_cases.description: Find old untagged manifests and prepare a reviewed deletion workflow.

prompt_templates.title: List Repositories
prompt_templates.prompt: Show a Python example that authenticates with DefaultAzureCredential and lists every repository in my Azure Container Registry.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Recent Manifests
prompt_templates.prompt: List manifests for [repository] from newest to oldest. Print each digest, tags, size, and last update time.

prompt_templates.title: Lock Production Images
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reviewed Python workflow that disables deletion and writes for [repository] and its [manifest]. Explain required permissions.

prompt_templates.title: Design Safe Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an asynchronous cleanup workflow for untagged manifests older than [days]. Include dry-run output, explicit confirmation, error handling, and client cleanup.

output_examples.input: List repositories and summarize the latest tags for each.
Find untagged manifests older than 30 days without deleting them.
output_examples.output: Dry run found 12 untagged manifests using 4.8 GB. No registry data was changed.

output_examples.input: Explain how to protect a production repository.
output_examples.output: Set repository deletion and write permissions to disabled, verify the target registry, and confirm the updated properties.

best_practices: Use Entra ID credentials and grant only the registry permissions required for each task.
Verify the registry endpoint, repository, tag, and digest before every mutation.
Use dry runs and explicit confirmation before cleanup or deletion.
anti_patterns: Do not embed registry credentials or access tokens in source code.
Do not delete by mutable tag when an immutable digest is available.
Do not run age-based cleanup without checking tags, retention requirements, and recovery options.

faq.question: Which authentication method should I use?
faq.answer: Use DefaultAzureCredential for private registries. Anonymous access is suitable only for public registries that permit it.

faq.question: Can this skill upload container images?
faq.answer: No upload example is included. The skill focuses on metadata operations and downloading manifests or blobs.

faq.question: Can it delete repositories and images?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented SDK methods can delete repositories, tags, and manifests when your identity has permission.

faq.question: Does it support asynchronous operations?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an asynchronous client example for listing repositories and closing credentials correctly.

faq.question: How should cleanup be tested?
faq.answer: Start with a dry run, inspect every candidate, verify tags and digests, then require explicit approval before deletion.

faq.question: What must be installed?
faq.answer: Install the Azure Container Registry package. Authentication examples also require the Azure Identity package.
